saints.name: St. Pelagia the Penitent
saints.title: Penitent
saints.shortBlurb: A celebrated dancer of Antioch who turned from a life of sin to a hidden life of penance…
biography: Pelagia's story is told by James, a deacon of the church of Heliopolis, who places her in the fifth century. The foremost actress and dancer of Antioch, she rode through the city laden with gold and pearls while a synod of bishops was gathered there, and her splendor provoked the bishop Nonnus to a sermon on the judgment.

Struck by his preaching, she sought baptism, was received under her birth name with the deaconess Romana as godmother, and distributed her wealth to the widows, orphans, and poor of the city. Then she vanished from Antioch in men's clothing, taking the name Pelagius, and built herself a cell on the Mount of Olives at Jerusalem.

There she lived three or four years in hidden penance, so wasted by austerity that at her death, about 457, the brethren who came to bury the supposed monk discovered a woman. Her relics drew pilgrims from Jericho and the Jordan valley. Remembered as a model of repentance, she is invoked as patron of penitents and, from her former calling, of actresses.
saints.knownFor: Conversion from a life of sin to penitential solitude.
